summary: We are testing whether adding a Python scalar fast-path to the `_check_hour_range` function in astropy's angle-parsing code can reduce workload runtime by avoiding expensive NumPy ufunc overhead when the input is a plain Python number (e.g., `int(15)`). The workload benchmarks this exact function 10×2000 times, and profiling shows NumPy scalar operations cost ~50-100× more than native Python equivalents for non-array inputs.
key_points: Single treatment arm (h-main): insert an `isinstance(hrs, np.ndarray)` guard at line 322 of `astropy/coordinates/angles/formats.py` so scalar inputs use `abs(hrs)` and plain comparisons instead of `np.any(np.abs(hrs))`, while the array path remains unchanged.

Prediction: workload mean runtime should decrease noticeably from the ~0.000145s baseline because the per-call cost drops from ~6.4µs (NumPy path) to ~0.08µs (Python builtins) — roughly 50-100× faster per invocation.

Confirmation criteria: mean runtime drops measurably and all 13 covering test files still pass. Refutation: if import/setup overhead dominates the benchmark or the isinstance check itself offsets gains, runtime stays flat.

Risk is low — the code change is a 5-line guard clause that preserves the existing array code path exactly; correctness is verified by the required test suite covering angle parsing, coordinate transforms, and sky-coord operations.
